sasha: Hey folks — running into a blocker on the migration guide PR. The example in the guide shows the canary config using `batch_size: auto` and says it 'prefers smaller latency', but runtime behaviour seems to pick bigger batches in low traffic. Can someone confirm whether the runtime rounds the auto batch target up or down when targets conflict?

mike: I can take a look. Quick Q: is this the snippet in the guide or the SDK example?

sasha: It's the guide snippet under 'Canary -> batching' (line ~45). Here's the exact YAML we're showing:```yaml
canary:
  mode: weighted
  batch_size: auto
  max_latency_ms: 120
```

jess: The runtime uses workload-aware batching. For `auto` it picks a target based on recent seq length distribution and latency SLOs. It then applies device-quantization rounding (power-of-two) for kernel choice which can push the *actual* batch higher.

sasha: That helps but the docs phrase 'prefers smaller latency' which implies it would bias toward smaller batches. If the kernel rounding can increase batch, that wording is misleading and will break the migration notes.

mike: Right — short answer: the runtime chooses a target that biases toward lower latency within the SLO, but kernel/quantization constraints can bump the effective batch up. So both are true. We should add a clarification.

sasha: @jess @mike if either of you can give a one-sentence authoritative line I can drop into the PR, that'd be great — reviewer is waiting and CI preview is green but we can't merge without the clarification.

jess: Proposed line: "When `batch_size: auto`, the runtime selects a latency-biased batch target that satisfies SLOs; hardware kernel and quantization alignment may cause the executed batch size to be rounded to a hardware-friendly value, which can increase per-batch throughput."

santiago: small wording nit: replace "executed batch size" with "effective batch size" to avoid confusion with user config.

jess: Good call. New line: "When `batch_size: auto`, the runtime selects a latency-biased batch target that satisfies SLOs; hardware kernel and quantization alignment may cause the effective batch size to be rounded to a hardware-friendly value, which can increase per-batch throughput."

sasha: Perfect. I'll paste that into the PR in the migration section and ping reviewers.

doc-preview-bot: Docs preview is available — https://preview.docs.redwood.ai/branches/sasha/migration-batching-clarify (renders in ~30s) :mag_right:

sasha: Pushed the line and requested reviews from @mike and @jess. CI shows linkcheck + lint passing.

ci-bot: CI: static-checks passed, linkcheck passed, docs-preview succeeded (build id: 202303-789)

mike: ACK — thanks. One more tiny thing: can we add a parenthetical example for kernel rounding? like "(e.g., rounds to next power-of-two for some kernels)"

sasha: added parenthetical and pushed. Leaving this as merge-on-approval. Thanks everyone :party_parrot:

jess: Thanks — merging once reviewers approve.

sasha: closing thread after merge.
